profileStep1Title: Step 1: Go to Your Steam Profile
profileStep1Description: Log into Steam and navigate to your profile page. You can do this by clicking on your username in the top navigation bar.
profileStep2Description: In the Edit Profile page, find and click on the 'Privacy Settings' option in the left sidebar.
profileStep3Title: Step 3: Update Your Game Details Privacy
profileStep3Description: In the Privacy Settings page, look for the 'Game details' section and set it to Public. You may also want to set your 'Friends List' to Public for a better experience.
profileStep3AlertDescription: Carefully review these settings before changing them.
profileStep4Description: After updating your settings, it may take up to 24 hours for the changes to take effect.
profilePrivacyConcernsDescription: We only access your public achievement data to provide our service. Making your game details public only allows others to see your games, achievements, and playtime.

aboutMissionParagraph1: Steam Vault was created with a simple goal: let gamers find their rarest achievements across the platform.
aboutMissionParagraph2: Achievements aren't always just milestones; they can represent hours of dedication, learning, practicing, and grinding. For most people, no one else will ever notice this. Steam Vault aims to change that.
aboutMissionParagraph3: Our platform is designed to celebrate your gaming journey, allowing you to view your achievements in a new light. We also aim to provide you with insights and other info to keep you going.

loadingScreenTitle1: Switching to your pistol is faster than reloading!
loadingScreenDescription1: While developing Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare (2007), Infinity Ward studied real special forces training manuals, focusing on radio chatter, movement tactics, and body language, to craft a cinematic yet tactically grounded experience.
loadingScreenDescription2: In Portal (2007), players are promised a literal cake, while being unknowingly lead to their demise. This tongue-in-cheek promise quickly evolved into an iconic reminder about empty incentives in game marketing.
loadingScreenTitle3: I've Spent Hours of My Life, Stomping... Koopas!
loadingScreenDescription3: Super Mario Bros. (1985) included a unused red "Koopa Troopa" enemy that had 2 lives. Leaked code for Super Mario All-Stars (1993) hints that this was planned as the default behavior for all Koopa Troopas.
loadingScreenDescription4: GoldenEye 007 (1997) was the first game to feature a first-person shooter multiplayer mode on a console. It set the standard for FPS games on consoles, influencing countless titles that followed.
loadingScreenTitle5: It's Dangerous to Go Alone! Take This!
loadingScreenDescription5: The original Legend of Zelda (1986) was one of the first console games to introduce a battery-backed save system, allowing players to record their extensive progress in an expansive open world. This feature redefined how adventure games were designed.
loadingScreenDescription6: The name "Zelda" (from The Legend of Zelda franchise) was inspired by Zelda Fitzgerald—the wife of author F. Scott Fitzgerald—giving the series an exotic and memorable title.
loadingScreenDescription7: The original Final Fantasy (1987), was conceived as developer Square's (later Square Enix) last-ditch effort during a financial crisis. Ironically, its unexpected success not only saved the company but also laid the groundwork for one of the most iconic and enduring RPG franchises.
